provenance.recorded: 2026-11-04, observed from a live three-way arbitration run (`python -X utf8 -m symmetry_court arbitrate --emit-expected-template`); the receipt is verdicts/lightsout3.verdict.json; the gate (`python -X utf8 -m symmetry_court selftest`) replays the case and compares these rows field-by-field
provenance.reading_guide: relabel row = engine's relabel frame (court-stamped copy; on this 9-action/9-bit model that frame resolves to the bitstring judge, which reads actions as bit flips -- a structural mismatch for a position-button system, recorded as the diagnostic column); fixed row = buttons pinned (--strict); the explicit declarations of g1/g4/g5 are adjudicated by the vendored engine directly (receipts in receipts/) and by the compare subcommand's declared-caliber gate arm; networkx columns = independent juror (the automorphism-set cross-check is skipped at 512 states per the court's scale guard, the O(E) direct edge-set check is the primary)

g1_rot90_map.claim: defendant A: rotating the 3x3 board 90 degrees clockwise and moving the buttons with it (the top-left button becomes the top-right button, and so on around the rotation) preserves the puzzle exactly -- buttons are bound to board positions, so the true symmetry carries its own button renaming; declared under the explicit caliber with per-element action maps

g1_rot90_map.note: the explicit declaration is adjudicated by the vendored engine directly (receipts/check.g1_rot90_map.json, engine run without --strict: pass, worst_tv 0.0, homomorphism_checked full) and by the compare subcommand's declared-caliber gate arm; the relabel column here resolves to the bitstring judge, which on this 9-action/9-bit model derives the action renaming from the state permutation itself (buttons are bit positions), so the relabel column passes in step with the explicit reading (contrast mini2048, where 4 actions on 8 bits made the same frame a structural mismatch); the fixed column is the buttons-pinned contrast

g2_rot90_nomap.claim: defendant B: the same 90-degree rotation with the buttons PINNED (the top-left button must stay the top-left button) -- the naive-intuition claim that 'the board looks the same rotated', filed deliberately under the fixed caliber to show it is the button renaming, not the state permutation, that makes defendant A true
